newsitem.title: CHINA: Visa introduces new debit card in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Visa introduces new debit card in Shanghai.

text.p: Visa International on Monday introduced a new debit card in Shanghai to be jointly issued by the Bank of China and Shanghai's Business News newspaper, Visa said in a statement.

The majority of payment cards in China are debit cards -- which first require a sum to be deposited in a bank account from which payments can be drawn -- rather than traditional credit cards, which give access to personal credit.
The new Visa Interlink card is the latest in a series of Great Wall payment cards issued by the Bank of China, one of China's major state-owned commercial banks, the statement said.
The card would be linked to local-currency yuan current accounts to be used for cash withdrawals from automatic teller machines and general settling of accounts, it said.
It can be used nationwide and would also be linked to overseas branches of the Bank of China, the statement said.
Visa currently has around 11 million cards on issue in China, the company said.
